```json
{"ranking": ["M5", "M6", "R3"], "fault": "M5 (op-amp tail current source) is undersized for its bias current. Its W/L of 2.02/2.34 gives Vdsat of about 0.55 V, but the tail node sits near 0.2 V because the input common-mode is fixed at about 0.9 V by the Rd divider. M5 is therefore pushed into triode, its current falls from the expected ~41 uA (4.1x mirror of M6) to 24.8 uA, and the amplifier bias and bandwidth shift, which moves f0. Fix by widening M5 (roughly 5-7x) or otherwise lowering its Vdsat so it stays saturated."}
```

Two caveats. The M5 triode finding is the clearest anomaly in the operating-point table, but the f0 error is about 10^6 (2.8e7 Hz simulated vs. 25–31 Hz target). The passive RC values alone give roughly 25 MHz, so the passive network itself may be scaled wrongly. If that is the case, no single amplifier device fully explains the spec miss, and the R3/C2 entries in the ranking deserve a closer look. M6 and R3 are the next candidates after M5.
